cards.text: Here's a song by David, king of Israel (2 Samuel 5:3), set to the tune of 'Do Not Destroy.' He turns to the rulers: 'Do you indeed speak justly, O rulers?' Then he asks, 'Do you judge uprightly, O sons of men?'

cards.question: David just asked the rulers if they speak justly and judge uprightly. What answer does he give?

answers.text: No they devise injustice in their hearts
Yes they judge the people fairly
He leaves the answer up to God

cards.text: And it's not just their hearts: with their hands the rulers mete out violence on the earth. Then David turns to the wicked and the liars.

cards.question: David says the wicked and the liars only start going astray once they grow up.

cards.text: Now David reaches for a picture. Their venom is like a snake's venom, like a cobra, but this cobra has one strange habit.

cards.question: In David's picture, what does the cobra do when the charmer plays his tune?

cards.text: The charmer skillfully weaves his spell, and that cobra refuses to hear his tune. Friend, that's ME with my oven timer: it plays its little song, and my ears are SHUT.
Then the song turns, and David prays straight to God: 'O God, shatter their teeth in their mouths…'

cards.question: David's prayer goes on to the lions. He asks the LORD to tame them so they lie down in peace.

cards.text: David keeps praying: may they vanish like water that runs off. GONE, like a fresh batch of cookies in the kitchen of the Millers, the family who carved my name into my handle.

cards.question: David asks that when the wicked draw the bow, their arrows will be blunted.

cards.text: Then come two more pictures, and this part is heavy: a slug that dissolves in its slime, and a woman's stillborn child.

cards.question: With the slug and the stillborn child, what does David ask for the wicked?

answers.text: That they never see the sun
That they live to see old age
That they find their way home

cards.text: Next David pictures pots sitting over a fire of burning thorns, green or dry. Friend, keep your eye on those pots, because this one happens FAST.

cards.question: Before the pots can even feel the burning thorns, green or dry, what will God do with the wicked?
Now the song turns to the righteous. David says they will rejoice when they see they are avenged.

cards.text: Then comes a hard, vivid picture. David says the righteous 'will wash their feet in the blood of the wicked.'

cards.question: Then people will say there is surely a ___ for the righteous
David started by asking if the rulers judge uprightly. At the end, people say there is surely someone who judges the earth. Who?
